title: Romberg retest improvement does not add stable symptom prediction beyond best stance time in two NHANES samples
abstract: In 2296 NHANES 2003–2004 adults who reached condition4, adding a linear retest-improvement term increased weighted Brier error for prior-year dizziness/balance/falling problems from 0.166208 to 0.166323; the source-and-target survey-bootstrap interval for baseline-minus-augmented error was [-0.001096, 0.000287]. Stable added prediction was not established.
